Same-base parity makes the midpoint base integral. The same-batch graph identity gives the exact midpoint mark even when original fibers have different affine directions elsewhere. Counting weights and at most 2^n occupied labels meet the finite theorem, including n=0.

Each retained centroid belongs to its original fiber. The ambient cut restricts either to a proper containing closed cut in that fiber’s affine q-plane or to all of it, including if it lies on the ambient boundary. The full-mass centroid case gives at least gamma_q a for the proper restriction. q=0 gives one count.

Summing over the selected marks yields 2^(-n) gamma_q a|P_max| in every cut at the same actual mark. Dividing by M keeps the factor M_max/M. With q=0 all nonempty fibers are singletons; with all positive intrinsic masses equal all mass is retained.
For x>0, the derivative of x log(1+1/x) is log(1+1/x)−1/(x+1)>0 by integrating 1/(1+t) over t from 0 to 1/x. Therefore gamma_q≥gamma_d for q≤d, with gamma_0=1.
